task_intent: Redesign Tessera arcade games and music service connections.

references.query: A snake game playing screen with a dark game board, score and directional controls
references.observed: A pale checkerboard, a small green snake with eyes, score above the board, and large separate Pause and End Game controls.
applied: Restrained checkerboard garden and a directional head with two eyes
Score and phase sit outside the playable grid
Explicit start and pause; separate accessible directional controls

references.query: A falling block puzzle game playing screen with a tall colorful board, next piece preview and score
references.observed: An ordered pale square grid with red and blue dimensional blocks, a separate upcoming purple shape, and minimal score/navigation chrome.
applied: Distinct inset well, softly bevelled blocks, and a permanent next-piece study
Quiet surrounding space gives the active piece and landing outline priority
Colour-independent letters and ghost outlines supplement piece colours

references.observed: A rotated music lesson with notation and a keyboard, not a falling-block puzzle.
references.excluded_reason: Returned by the search but did not inform this game.

applied: Controls at least 44 points with visible and haptic press feedback
Arrow keys map to directions; pause uses Space; Tetris hard drop uses Return
Compact artwork at accessibility text sizes keeps controls reachable
VoiceOver board summaries and explicit custom actions
Received game state is drawn without speculative animation; Reduce Motion removes control scaling
Ten cleared lines advance a level and increase falling speed
Complete rows clear; a stack reaching the top ends the round
Persistent ghost landing position gives deliberate placement feedback
Separate rotation and immediate drop actions

composition.snake: Normalized square garden at x=6/64, y=11/64, side=52/64 with the full 32×32 grid. Header and score never cover play cells.
composition.tetris: Normalized 10×20 well at x=4/64, y=2/64 with 3/64 cells, plus next/score/lines/level sidebar. Native and Python use identical positions and piece colours.
composition.adaptations: True64 omits inset block letters and the fine well grid. Compact 3×5 HUD glyphs preserve all labels and values. Larger renders retain the same geometry; software RGB cannot certify the physical LEDs.
